title: Safehouse and Debt
premise: Mirabel Sandoval, a disgraced intelligence analyst hiding in a government safehouse after blowing the whistle on a covert assassination program, discovers the property has been listed online — interior photos and all — meaning someone inside the protection apparatus sold her location. As buyers tour the house and a cleanup team closes in, she realizes her only leverage is the encrypted drive she stole: proof implicating Deputy Director Callum Voss. Trading it means exposing herself to prosecution; keeping it means dying quietly. In the end, Mirabel broadcasts the evidence publicly rather than trade it, sacrificing her anonymity but forcing Voss's arrest and reclaiming her own name.
about_author: Ines Pemberton is a former compliance investigator who spent a decade auditing institutions that preferred not to be audited. She writes paranoid, morally tangled thrillers from a farmhouse whose previous owners, she insists, were never fully explained.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Scrolling real estate sites at 3 a.m., she finds the safehouse for sale — twelve photos of rooms only she and two handlers should know. The emotional beat is cold recognition: invisibility was an illusion, and someone she trusted built the illusion.

chapters.title: Handler Ghosts
chapters.summary: Mirabel confronts her handler, Dane Okafor, by burner phone; he denies knowledge but his voice cracks. POV alternates briefly to the buyer's agent noticing a woman watching the open house. Beat: loyalty begins to fracture under the first question.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, Three Exits
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Mirabel's POV: how she was burned from each agency, culminating in the incident that cost a colleague's life. Emotional beat: guilt as engine — she stayed silent too long once before and won't again.

chapters.title: The Drive
chapters.summary: Present day. Mirabel retrieves the encrypted drive hidden in the crawlspace, reviewing what it contains: Voss's authorization signatures on three 'disappearances.' Beat: dread mixed with grim purpose — the secret is worth killing for, and she holds it.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Mirabel watches the open house from across the street; among the tourists she spots a man photographing sightlines, not rooms. POV shifts to the watcher, a fixer named Corliss, cataloguing her habits. Beat: the hunt has already begun.

chapters.title: Okafor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dane's POV. He audits who had access to the listing photos and finds Voss's office requested them 'for asset reassessment.' He must choose between reporting it and protecting Mirabel. Beat: loyalty tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: Buyer Number Four
chapters.summary: A cash buyer makes an above-ask offer within hours — a shell company Mirabel traces to a Voss-linked foundation. Beat: rising panic; they aren't selling the house, they're buying her burial plot.

chapters.title: The Incident, Revisited
chapters.summary: Second flashback, dual POV of Mirabel and the dead colleague, Elena Ruiz, through recovered emails. Reveals Elena discovered the program first. Beat: grief sharpening into resolve — this debt is personal.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Corliss approaches Mirabel openly at a diner: trade the drive for a quiet exit and a new identity, or be collected in forty-eight hours. Beat: temptation offered cleanly, which makes it more terrifying.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Mirabel consults a retired journalist, Ada Brandt, about going public. Ada warns that leaks die without corroboration and distribution. Beat: hope flickering against the machinery of silence.

chapters.title: Dane's Choice
chapters.summary: Voss summons Dane, offering him Mirabel's old job if he delivers the drive. Dane stalls, then secretly copies the access logs proving the listing leak. Beat: loyalty tips toward truth, at personal ruin.

chapters.title: Forty-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Ticking-clock chapter, Mirabel's POV: she preps contingencies, mails a decoy package, memorizes the drive's contents. Beat: controlled terror; she plans her own funeral logistics.

chapters.title: The Decoy Burns
chapters.summary: Corliss intercepts the decoy, realizes it's fake, and escalates — the collection team mobilizes early. POV Corliss, revealing he keeps insurance files on every client including Voss. Beat: predator becoming potential ally.

chapters.title: Safehouse Siege
chapters.summary: Mirabel returns for the last cache and finds the house occupied. A tense cat-and-mouse escape through the listing's own photographed rooms. Beat: the house that exposed her nearly ends her.

chapters.title: Ada's Condition
chapters.summary: Ada agrees to publish but demands Mirabel go on record with her real name — no anonymity, no deniability. Beat: the central bargain crystallizes: truth requires surrendering the self.

chapters.title: Voss Ascendant
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He briefs his directorate on a 'compromised asset,' positioning Mirabel as a foreign agent. Beat: power's corruption shown as bureaucratic fluency in lies.

chapters.title: The Trade Offer
chapters.summary: Final negotiation: Voss offers full immunity, Elena's case reopened, a life back — for the drive. Mirabel almost says yes. Beat: the lowest moment; justice inside the law dangled like bait.

chapters.title: Elena's Voice
chapters.summary: Mirabel plays Elena's recovered voicemail — 'if I disappear, it wasn't an accident' — and understands trading the drive buries Elena twice. Beat: grief transmuted into decision.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. With Ada and Dane, Mirabel releases the drive, the logs, and her sworn statement simultaneously across independent outlets minutes before the collection team arrives. Beat: white-knuckle execution, all threads converging.

chapters.title: Collection, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Corliss, reading the news, stands down and hands federal agents his insurance file on Voss rather than collect Mirabel. Beat: even mercenaries hedge when truth goes nuclear.

chapters.title: Hearings
chapters.summary: Resolution part one: Voss arrested; Mirabel testifies under her own name, prosecuted for theft but vindicated on substance. Dane accepts his consequences. Beat: justice outside the law forcing justice inside it.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Mirabel's POV. Months later, in a small apartment with curtains open, she sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident. Final beat: the debt paid, the name reclaimed, the window unshuttered.
